name: Meridian Munitions Wheelgun-38 'Roundhouse'
description:
The Meridian Munitions Wheelgun-38 is a six-shot double-action revolver chambered in .38 Special, built with a carbon steel frame and a four-inch barrel. It is the cheapest revolver available in GLMZ, manufactured using the same cost-minimization approach that defines all Meridian Munitions products. The finish is a flat black oxide that provides minimal corrosion resistance, and the grips are hard rubber with no contouring.

The Roundhouse exists because a significant portion of GLMZ's the Gray Zone population distrusts semi-automatic pistols. Revolvers are mechanically simpler — no magazines to lose, no slides to rack, no safeties to forget. For residents with minimal firearms training, the revolver's simplicity is its primary feature: load it, point it, pull the trigger. The heavy double-action trigger pull serves as both a safety mechanism and a quality-control compromise.

The weapon's reliability is its saving grace. Where a Payday might jam, a Roundhouse will fire. The .38 Special round provides adequate stopping power against unarmored targets, and the six-round cylinder doesn't require counting rounds or managing reloads under stress. For the Gray Zone residents who want 'a gun that works when I need it to work,' the Roundhouse delivers on that promise and nothing more.

tactical_use: A basic defensive revolver offering simplicity and reliability at the cost of capacity and reloading speed. The double-action trigger is heavy but consistent. Six rounds of .38 Special provide adequate stopping power for unarmored threats. No external safety to disengage under stress. The revolver's simplicity makes it nearly malfunction-proof in untrained hands.
cultural_context: The Roundhouse is the Gray Zone purist's firearm. Its owners tend to view semi-automatic pistols with suspicion — too many moving parts, too many things that can go wrong. There's a generational divide at play: older the Gray Zone residents overwhelmingly prefer revolvers, while younger residents gravitate toward semi-automatics. The Roundhouse is the old guard's weapon of choice.
story_hooks: An elderly the Gray Zone shopkeeper defends their store with a Roundhouse and becomes an unlikely folk hero — but the attention draws scrutiny to their past that they've spent decades hiding.
A batch of Roundhouses is discovered with barrels bored out to accept .357 Magnum — a dangerous modification that the weapons weren't built to withstand.
physical_description: The Roundhouse is a utilitarian six-shot revolver with a stubby four-inch barrel and a carbon steel frame finished in flat black oxide that's begun to show surface rust in places. Hard rubber grips—unpadded and sharp-edged—wrap the grip frame, and the cylinder rotates with a mechanical click that feels more honest than reliable. It's the kind of gun that looks like it was stamped out yesterday and will look the same way in ten years, assuming it doesn't jam first.
